meaning: (1) the son of Appoline; (2) the son of Abel, from dim. Abelin, sharpened to Apelin; (3) the son of Lyon, a Welsh personal name, whence the patr. ap-Lyon
author_comment: The homily 'Against the perils of Idolatry' says, 'All diseases have their special saints as gods, the curers of them: the toothache, St. Appoline.' This was the usual English form of Appolonia, a martyr at Alexandria, who, among other tortures, had all her teeth beaten out. It was a popular girl's name, and survived the Reformation. (2) cf. Apps for Abbs, or Epps for Ebbs. (3) This undoubtedly became Applin, and represents the Applins of cos. Somerset, Hereford, and south-west England generally; cf. Applejohn.
source: Register of St. Peter, Cornhill, 1538-1774 (Harleian Society)
record_text: 1593. Bapt.—Apeline, d. John Morris, clothworker: St. Peter, Cornhill.
